steps.text: Combine gelatin, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and salt in a heavy saucepan; stir in condensed milk and beaten eggs, mixing well. Let stand one minute, then place on burner over low heat, stirring constantly until gelatin dissolves and mixture thickens, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat.
Stir in pumpkin until thoroughly combined; pour mixture into graham cracker crust. Chill for at least 3 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: No-Bake Pumpkin Pie
raw_recipe.description: This no-bake pumpkin pie has a rich and creamy filling in a prepared graham cracker crust. An excellent make-ahead dessert for the holidays!

video.description: This is the only pumpkin pie recipe you’ll need this fall. In this video, Nicole shows you how to make no-bake pumpkin pie with an easy homemade filling that comes together on the stovetop in just 10 minutes. For some pumpkin pie cheesecake vibes, this recipe also features a graham cracker crust that lets you show off the very best of both worlds. Once refrigerated and set, top with fresh whipped cream and freshly grated nutmeg, then enjoy every perfect bite of this quintessential fall dessert.
video.name: How to Make No-Bake Pumpkin Pie

review.reviewBody: WOW! Just bought an antique stove, but it wasn't installed for Thanksgiving. So for the holiday dessert, we decided to try a couple no-bake pies. This pumpkin pie is absolutely delicious. You wouldn't know it wasn't baked judging by it's taste and consistency; in fact this was superior. And I've baked a lot of pumpkin pies! I won't bake a pumpkin pie again, as this pie was creamier, filled the pie crust better, and in fact was easier to prepare. I usually add more spices than recipes call for, but this recipe was just right, nice and spicy. Thank you Cathy.

I love this recipe! Not only is it incredibly easy, it is delicious! I did add a bit of ground cloves and allspice along with the other spices; however, this was not necessary as the mixture was beautiful beforehand - I just love cloves with my pumpkin. I didn't have a graham cracker crust (for some reason they aren't sold in Australia that I am aware of) so I used some mini tart shells...they were so cute and everyone LOVED them. I will definitely keep this recipe in my arsenal and use it from now on! Thank you so much for posting!

Used a no bake graham cracker crust and made this pie in 6 half-pint jars. Substituted 3/4 c Splenda and 12 oz evaporated milk for the sweetened condensed milk. Worked great for my diabetic hubs and he'll have something special for dessert on Thanksgiving. Will use Splenda in the whipped cream topping when we open his jars!

Thanks for this tasty solution.

I made two the first one came out okay it was just a tad bit on the mushy side. The second one I followed the recipe but instead of just adding pumpkin and put it immediately in a pie crust instead I cooked the pumpkin with the other ingredients for an extra 5 to 7 minutes and it thickened the pumpkin up and it also took out that raw pumpkin taste.

So easy! Just added a tbsp of vanilla though- that's the only change. Be sure to add the beaten eggs a little at a time to make sure they don't scramble! I made a day ahead and the consistency was perfect!

Well, I have to admit it was easy! I did need one substitution, as I only had a half cup of pumpkin. I mashed a half a banana and threw it in! Can’t even tell it’s there. I blended the whole lot after cooking the egg and milk mixture and poured it into premade miniature graham cracker crusts. What a wonderful recipe, It may be my new ‘go to’ as it was so fast!!

I had to make mini pumpkin pies for a bridal shower and because I didn't want to overcook the pies or burn the crust, I made one batch and filled pre-cooked crusts. I topped the mini pies off with a structured whip cream. (See photo) this recipe was amazing and delicious! I added 1/4 tsp of ground cloves to the pie mix as well. I'm definitely doing these again! Thanks for the great recipe!!

Like many others, my oven was just too full for anything else, so I went looking for gold, and found it with this recipe. The pie I made is one of the best I have ever had, in my opinion. I didn't have any gelatin, but added in an additional egg and it was lovely. I normally don't use canned pumpkin, but found some on sale so that's what I used. My hubby is always suspicious because I have used sweet potatoes, butternut squash, or other squashes and he wants to make sure it is the real thing. He ate two pieces, then began to nibble just a little more. Then he had more for breakfast. I'll use this again.

Great recipe! Important to thicken up the gelatin mixture. I cooked on medium for about 5 extra minutes & that did it. Great spice flavor! I will make again. I made day beforehand. Pie was set & easy to serve.

This recipe is awesome! I made it and everyone loved it. I used this recipe a second time but modified it instead of canned pumpkin I made a blueberry peach puree in my food processor and only used cinnamon and a little vanilla extract. It turned out awesome as well. Next I'm trying raspberry apple I'll update with how that turns out. Awesome recipe!
WOW!! Best flavor I've ever had in a pumpkin pie, and as a general rule of thumb pumpkin is my least favorite pie. Super easy and I used a gingersnap crust. Perfection!!!
Delicious, fast and easy! Easy ingredients to. I hate when I have to go get just one or two ingredients to complete a recipe. Chances are, I'll never need the ingredients for anything else!!
Better than a normal pumpkin pie! Everyone always loves this pie when I make it. Flavor is amazing, recipe is easy to follow too!

This recipe was disgusting and a complete waste of time and money. It was very runny and tasted too much like nutmeg. Not even whipped cream helped with the taste. I'm assuming bots are the reason it's rated 4.6 stars.
I have never been a fan of pie crust , but I love pumpkin pie filling so my first Thanksgiving with my husband I tried this recipe that was 25 years ago and we have had it every year . Love it !
I used a premade walnut pie crust which was good.
Excellent recipe. Tasty with all the cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger
I'm not a fan of this one, but it's worth a try.

Easy to make. I think you need a higher heat than low to help the gelatin set better.
Loved the taste!
